results.title: The signed encoding of integers
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The *signed encoding* $\operatorname{enc}:\mathbb Z\to\mathbb N$ and its *decoding* $\operatorname{dec}:\mathbb N\to\mathbb Z$ are \operatorname{dec}(c)=\begin{cases}c/2,&c\text{ even},\\-(c+1)/2,&c\text{ odd}.\end{cases}$$ A tuple $c=(c_0,c_1,c_2,c_3,c_4)\in\mathbb N^5$ of precision inputs decodes, in this fixed order, to $(n,\kappa,a,l,j)=(\operatorname{dec}c_0,\dots,\operatorname{dec}c_4)\in\mathbb Z^5$.

results.title: The signed encoding is a bijection
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: $\operatorname{dec}(\operatorname{enc}(n))=n$ for every $n\in\mathbb Z$ and $\operatorname{enc}(\operatorname{dec}(c))=c$ for every $c\in\mathbb N$. Moreover $\operatorname{enc}(n)$ is even exactly when $n\ge0$, and $|\operatorname{dec}(c)|=\lceil c/2\rceil$.

results.title: Admissibility of nonzero indices
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Assume $P_0$ has infinite order in $E(K_0)$. Then every $k\in\mathbb Z\setminus\{0\}$ is admissible. Consequently, for $c\in\mathbb N^5$ passing the early tests of the precision relation, the indices $l,a,j$ are admissible, and $\operatorname{accepts}(c)$ holds if and only if the closeness and precision tests hold.

results.title: Elements of norm zero
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For $u,v\in\mathbb Q$, if $u^2-2v^2=0$ then $u=v=0$. Equivalently, an element $z$ of $K_0$ with $\operatorname N(z)=0$ is zero, and for $Y\in\mathbb Z[s]$ with $Y\ne0$ the integer $\operatorname N(Y)=Y\bar Y$ is nonzero. Hence every division by an element of $K_0$ in the precision computation can be guarded by the exact test $\operatorname N\ne0$ on integer components.

results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The *decision program* is the total function $\mathrm{decide}:\mathbb N^5\to\{\mathrm{true},\mathrm{false}\}$ computed by the following steps on $c\in\mathbb N^5$; every quantity is an integer, an element of $\mathbb Z[s]$ (a pair of integers) or a natural number, and every test is exact.

results.title: Correctness of the decision program
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every $c\in\mathbb N^5$, $\mathrm{decide}(c)=\mathrm{true}\iff\operatorname{accepts}(c)$. The program terminates on every input, including every early rejection.
